title: Images, files and covers
p: Sometimes an image says more than a paragraph. Add screenshots, documents and other files to your notes, then use icons and covers to make frequently used pages easy to recognize.

ol.li: Choose Image from the slash menu and select a file.
Drag an image from Finder into the document.
Paste an image from the clipboard with ⌘ V. On macOS, ⌘ ⌃ ⇧ 4 captures a selection to the clipboard.

p: JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP and BMP are supported, up to 20 MB per image. The file is copied into your documents folder, so moving the original does not break the note.

img.caption: An image with a caption underneath

p: Click an image to select it, then drag a corner handle to resize it while keeping its proportions. Use the toolbar to align it left, center or right.
Choose Crop, adjust the frame, then save the crop or double-click inside it. Cropping leaves the original file intact, so you can reset the image later.

img.caption: The middle of the same image, cropped without changing its source

p: Use the caption control to add a source, a date or a short explanation. Captions are included when you export.
Click a selected image again to open the viewer.

Content pasted from a website may reference images by URL. In Settings › General, you can enable automatic downloading. When it is disabled, remote images remain placeholders until you choose to load them.
Choose the file block from the slash menu or drag a file into a document. PDFs, office documents, audio, video and archives are copied into your documents folder.
h2: Three ways to display a file
p: A compact card shows the file's icon, name and size.
Show supported content directly in your note: PDFs, office documents, images, text and code. Audio files can show a player.
Mention a file within a sentence, like this reference: .

ul.li: Click a selected file again to open macOS Quick Look. The fullscreen control does the same.
Use Download to save a copy outside your documents folder.
MP4, MOV and M4V support video previews. Other formats can be kept as cards and opened externally.

p: Hover above a title and add an icon to choose an emoji. Click an existing icon to search, browse categories, pick a random one or remove it.
These guides use the default icons. In the sidebar, a page with child documents shows a folder icon so you can recognize its place in the tree.
A cover is a banner above the document title. This guide has one; most of the others do not.
Hover above the title and add a cover. Choose an image from the built-in gallery or upload your own. Wide images, around 2000 × 400 pixels, work well.

column.p: Browse gradients, landscapes and other designs, or let the random option choose one.
Use a photograph, an illustration or a project banner from your Mac.

p: Hover over the cover to replace it, reposition it or remove it. Drag while repositioning to choose the visible area, then confirm.

callout.p: Covers appear on Home cards. Different covers help you spot familiar documents at a glance.
